entries.text:
Trailing zeros are formed by factors of 10.

Since 10 = 2 x 5 and factors of 2 are available in excess in n!, we only count factors of 5.

{factorFiveCountLatex}

Therefore, the number of trailing zeros in {n}! is {answer}.

families.name: Count Trailing Zeros In Factorial Expressions

entries.text:
Evaluate the contribution of factors of 5 from each factorial term.

{factorialExpressionLatex}

The total number of available factors of 5 gives the trailing-zero count.

Hence the answer is {answer}.

families.name: Smallest Number Whose Factorial Has Given Trailing Zeros

entries.text:
A trailing zero requires one factor 2 and one factor 5.

Prime-factorize the base.

{powerFactorizationLatex}

Count complete pairs of 2 and 5.

Hence the number of trailing zeros is {answer}.

families.name: Determine Change In Trailing Zeros After Multiplication

entries.text:
Prime-factorize the numbers.

{productFactorizationLatex}

Count the total factors of 2 and 5.

The smaller count determines the number of trailing zeros.

Hence the answer is {answer}.
